newsitem.title: UK: Cox seeks to buy Names capacity.
newsitem.headline: Cox seeks to buy Names capacity.

text.p: Cox Insurance Holdings Plc said on Monday it is to seek to buy 100 million stg of capacity from Names - the traditional backers of the Lloyd's insurance market - on three insurance syndicates it manages.
Prices for each one stg of capacity for the 1998 year of account on syndicates 218, 1485 and 1176 range from 13 pence to 40 pence.
The move is in line with the group's strategy, which it has repeatedly stated, of integrating Names into Cox.

Chief executive Michael Dawson said the offer represented the highest prices quoted at Lloyd's to date in such an offer and was around double last year's average auction prices quoted for capacity on Cox managed syndicates.
"The prices offered also represent a substantial premium on the first 1997 capacity auction prices," added Dawson.
The maximum payable will be 22 million stg and the company is seeking to offer Names an alternative of taking shares in Cox.
The offer will not require fresh capital from existing shareholders but is subject to Lloyd's approval.
